## Two points from the literature {#two-sentences-worth-keeping}

::: {.claimcard}
"the common single-path analyses in social and behavioural research should not be simply assumed to be robust to alternative analyses" [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]
:::

::: {.claimcard}
A blueprint: precise question → causal reasoning (DAG) → multiverse → sensitivity analysis [@AuspurgBruderl2021HasCredibilitySocial]
:::

::: {.small}
- Same-conclusion robustness and same-*number* robustness are different bars
- Justifiability is the criterion – choose with reasons, show the spread
:::

::: notes
The first point comes from the article on the robustness study, that single-path analyses should not simply be assumed to be robust. Today the preregistration protected your choice from being opportunistic, but it gave your declared dot no special status within the curve, since the declared path is still one path among eight hundred and sixty-four, so a report needs the declared path and the space around it together. From Auspurg and Brüderl comes the constructive sequence that we followed: a precise question, explicit assumptions, the multiverse and the analysis of sensitivity. Keep the two standards of robustness apart in your own writing, the same conclusion, reached by seventy-four per cent of the reanalyses in the robustness study, and the same number, reached by thirty-four, and say which one you mean when you claim robustness.
:::

## What you take with you {.smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Yours now.** A rendered report with its preregistration block. An estimand statement and a causal graph that you wrote yourself. Two dots on the class chart, one exploratory from Task 4 and one preregistered from Task 5.
- **Read.** The three *Nature* papers of 2026 [@MiskeEtAl2026InvestigatingReproducibilitySocial; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness; @TynerEtAl2026InvestigatingReplicabilitySocial], the glossary [@NosekEtAl2025BriefGlossaryTerms], @AuspurgBruderl2021HasCredibilitySocial, @LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand, @LakensEtAl2026ThereOnlyOne and @Teney2016DoesEUEconomic.
- **Explore.** The companion modules of the case study, among them panel data, causal graphs, the multiverse debate, and repositories and preregistration. R, the IDE, Quarto, and Git and GitHub on the AR4DS website. The data of the robustness study. The documentation of `fixest` and `ggdag`.
- **Keep going locally.** The research-software and open-research teams at your university, and a ReproducibiliTea journal club near you.
- Everything is on the workshop's website, and everything is open – fork any of it
:::

::: {.urlbox}
codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-eu
:::

::: notes
You take home a rendered report with a preregistration block in it, an estimand statement and a causal graph that you wrote for a published claim, and two dots on the class chart, one exploratory from Task 4 and one declared in Task 5. The workshop's website, at the address on the screen, holds everything else: the readings, the data, the companion modules, the reading on the specification curve and the full SCORE dossier on the paper. To keep the habit alive wherever you work, most universities have a team of research software engineers and an open-research or data service in the library that run training of this kind, and ReproducibiliTea journal clubs meet at many universities.
:::
